title: Per-biome geometry styles — distinct edge / corner shapes per terrain family (grass undulates, path curves, stone bevels)
intent: S176 shipped the grass family using the SAME 4 procedural builders as soft-block. Different biomes (grass, path, stone, dirt, floor) should have visibly DISTINCT edge geometry that reads as their material — grass tufts undulate at the edge, stone tiles bevel sharply, dirt edges crumble irregularly, path curves smoothly, floor stays flat with subtle panel seams. Currently every family inherits the same crate/pallet/barrel/drum shapes from soft-block builders — a 'grass' cell looks like a wooden crate dyed green. This story: ship 4-5 distinct builders PER family (5 families × 5 builders = ~25 builders total). Each family declares its own builders module; the Wang lookup table from GDP-2026-05-29-004 still applies (same 16-bitmask logic, family-specific meshes).
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-29 — 'изгибы краев для разных типов биомов отличались, чтоб смотрелось органично'. Current state: grass family shares geometry with soft-block family — every biome looks like wooden crates in different colours. Marked `should` because the visual identity gap is significant for arena variety (the GDD's 'toy-scale industrial diorama' aesthetic needs RECOGNISABLE biomes, not colour-shifted crates).
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: GDP-2026-05-29-004 (Wang rotation fix) — that establishes the 5-builder-per-family pattern this story populates with biome-specific geometry.
FILE STRUCTURE — per-family builder modules:
examples/kaboom-crew/src/biomes/grass-variants.ts (rewrite S176 to be grass-specific)
examples/kaboom-crew/src/biomes/path-variants.ts (NEW)
examples/kaboom-crew/src/biomes/stone-variants.ts (NEW)
examples/kaboom-crew/src/biomes/dirt-variants.ts (NEW)
examples/kaboom-crew/src/biomes/floor-variants.ts (refactor existing flat-floor + S172 theme palette)
BIOME GEOMETRY STYLES (4-5 builders per family, distinct from other families):
GRASS family — soft, undulating, organic:
Variant 0 (edge) — flat green top + grass-blade vertices tilting OUTWARD on the open edge (small Y bumps on the non-same-family side). Visual: 'grass meadow ends here, blades flatten at the edge'.
Variant 1 (corner) — two open edges with grass blades tilting outward AT THE ANGLE between them. Smooth concave inner curve.
Variant 2 (filler) — surrounded — flat green with maximum blade density (Y-noise vertex displacement). Visual: 'thick grass interior'.
Variant 3 (isolated) — single tuft — small rounded mound with grass blades all around.
Variant 4 (straight wall) — long ribbon of grass — blades tilt outward on BOTH open faces.
Material: vertex-coloured warm green primary, darker stem at bottom edge.
PATH family — smooth, curving:
Variant 0 (edge) — packed dirt with a SMOOTH CURVED edge sloping down to ground level on the open side. Convex curve.
Variant 1 (corner) — two smoothly-curved edges meeting at a convex apex.
Variant 2 (filler) — flat brown packed dirt, mild speckle of stones (vertex colour spots).
Variant 3 (isolated) — single round disc with sloped edges all around.
Variant 4 (straight wall) — long lane with smooth sloped edges on both sides — path read.
Material: warm brown primary, scattered stone vertex-colour dots.
STONE family — geometric, beveled:
Variant 0 (edge) — flat top + 45° beveled edge dropping to ground on the open side. Sharp geometry.
Variant 1 (corner) — two beveled edges meeting at a vertical corner edge. Geometric.
Variant 2 (filler) — flat stone tile with mortar seam pattern (vertex-colour lines).
Variant 3 (isolated) — single stone slab with beveled edges all around.
Variant 4 (straight wall) — long stone strip with beveled edges + mortar seam down the middle.
Material: cool grey primary, dark mortar lines, slight rim highlight from edge bevel.
DIRT family — irregular, crumbled:
Variant 0 (edge) — soft displaced edge with random vertex displacement on the open side. Irregular.
Variant 1 (corner) — two irregular edges meeting at a soft convex angle.
Variant 2 (filler) — flat brown with multiple subtle vertex bumps (texture-y feel).
Variant 3 (isolated) — single mound with crumbly all-around edges.
Variant 4 (straight wall) — long crumbled strip.
Material: warm brown earth, vertex-colour mottling.
FLOOR family — clean, industrial:
Variant 0 (edge) — flat tile with panel seam along the wall-adjacent edge.
Variant 1 (corner) — flat tile with panel seams on two adjacent sides.
Variant 2 (filler) — flat tile, NO seams (just the bottom-shadow trick + slight vertex colour).
Variant 3 (isolated) — flat tile with panel seams all four sides.
Variant 4 (straight wall) — flat tile with panel seams on two opposite sides.
Material: cream/grey theme-tinted, optional emissive accent on panel seams.
REGISTRATION (examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/register-wang-families.ts — extends S170 registration):
Each family registers with its own 5 builders + the SHARED 16-entry lookup table from GDP-2026-05-29-004.
Engine Wang resolver picks the builder via lookup table → applies rotation.
PALETTE INTERACTION:
Each builder accepts a palette parameter (matching the S172 theme-aware block-palette pattern).

Theme switching (S171) tints biome geometry — e.g. lab theme has bluer-tinged grass (more like lab-floor moss?) — or sticks to natural family palettes regardless of theme. Default: natural family palettes UNCHANGED by theme; theme tints only walls + accent emissive.
PROCBOMBER-BENCH INTEGRATION:
Bench gains a 'Biome family' dropdown — preview each family's 5 variants in a row, see the distinct geometries.
Bench shows a small 3×3 grid demo with the dropdown's family — see variants 0/1/2 tiled together.
PROTOTYPE ARENA (this story):

Update `examples/kaboom-crew/scenes/grassland.scene.json` (introduced in pending GDP-028-012) — terrainmap mixes grass + path + dirt + stone in a meadow-with-path layout. Demonstrates 4 visibly distinct biomes side-by-side.
Wall-shadow Wang layer (still pending in GDP-028-012) — note as out-of-scope for THIS story; the multi-family biomes ship independent of the shadow overlay.
TESTS:
Each family registers with 5 builders.
Variant 0 of grass and variant 0 of stone produce DIFFERENT vertex counts (or different vertex displacement profiles) — they don't share geometry.
Grass variant 4 (straight wall) renders distinct from soft-block variant 4 (plank wall).
VISUAL QA:
Load grassland arena → grass + path + stone + dirt visibly distinct. Edges curve / bevel / undulate / crumble differently per family.
Take a screenshot of a row containing all 5 families (one cell each, straight strip) → 5 visually distinct cells, no two look like 'colour-shifted crates'.
Camera zoom-in → biome-specific geometry detail visible (grass blade displacement, stone bevel angle, etc.).
PERFORMANCE: each builder produces ~150-300 vertices. 5 families × 5 builders = 25 procedural meshes cached. ~6KB total mesh data. Negligible.
OUT OF SCOPE:
Inter-family BLENDED transitions (grass softly fades into path). Sharp transitions per the GDP-028-012 v1 rule.
Cliff-face Wang autotiling (GDP-2026-05-29-006 separately).
Wall-shadow overlay Wang layer (pending GDP-028-012 cleanup).
CC0 asset variants — procedural only.
Multi-cell biome patches (e.g. 2x2 cell grass clusters that share a single mesh). Per-cell only.
Animated biome (rippling grass in wind). Static only.
Per-theme biome palette overrides. Natural family palettes only.
